sanskrit: purā stimitaniḥśabdam ākāśam acalopamam naṣṭacandrārkapavanaṃ prasuptam iva saṃbabhau
english: In the beginning space was motionless and soundless, like a mountain at rest; with moon, sun, and wind alike extinguished, it seemed as though asleep.

sanskrit: tataḥ salilam utpannaṃ tamasīvāparaṃ tamaḥ tasmāc ca salilotpīḍād udatiṣṭhata mārutaḥ
english: Then water came into being, like one darkness arising within another darkness; and from the pressure of that swelling water the wind sprang up.

sanskrit: yathā bhājanam acchidraṃ niḥśabdam iva lakṣyate tac cāmbhasā pūryamāṇaṃ saśabdaṃ kurute 'nilaḥ
english: Just as an unbroken vessel appears to be silent, yet when it is being filled with water the moving air within makes a sound,

sanskrit: tathā salilasaṃruddhe nabhaso 'nte nirantare bhittvārṇavatalaṃ vāyuḥ samutpatati ghoṣavān
english: so too, when the unbroken vault of the firmament was wholly shut in by water, the wind, breaking through the floor of the ocean, surged upward with a roar.

sanskrit: sa eṣa carate vāyur arṇavotpīḍasaṃbhavaḥ ākāśasthānam āsādya praśāntiṃ nādhigacchati
english: This wind, born of the churning pressure of the ocean, ranges abroad; though it reaches the region of space, it finds no rest there.

sanskrit: tasmin vāyvambusaṃgharṣe dīptatejā mahābalaḥ prādurbhavaty ūrdhvaśikhaḥ kṛtvā vitimiraṃ nabhaḥ
english: In that friction of wind and water there appears a being of blazing splendor and mighty power, its flames leaping upward, making the heavens free of darkness.

sanskrit: agniḥ pavanasaṃyuktaḥ khāt samutpatate jalam so 'gnir mārutasaṃyogād ghanatvam upapadyate
english: Fire, joined with the wind, draws water up out of the sky; and that fire, through its union with the wind, comes to take on density.

sanskrit: tasyākāśe nipatitaḥ snehas tiṣṭhati yo 'paraḥ sa saṃghātatvam āpanno bhūmitvam upagacchati
english: The other unctuous residue of it that falls and remains within space, having attained solidity, passes into the state of earth.

sanskrit: rasānāṃ sarvagandhānāṃ snehānāṃ prāṇināṃ tathā bhūmir yonir iha jñeyā yasyāṃ sarvaṃ prasūyate
english: Earth is to be known here as the womb of all flavors, all scents, all unctuous things, and of all living creatures; in her all things are brought forth.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca ete te dhātavaḥ pañca brahmā yān asṛjat purā āvṛtā yair ime lokā mahābhūtābhisaṃjñitaiḥ
english: Bharadvāja said: These are the five elements which Brahmā created of old, by which these worlds are enveloped, and which are designated the great elements.

sanskrit: yad āsṛjat sahasrāṇi bhūtānāṃ sa mahāmatiḥ pañcānām eva bhūtatvaṃ kathaṃ samupapadyate
english: Since that great-minded one created creatures by the thousands, how is it that elemental nature belongs to these five alone?

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca amitānāṃ mahāśabdo yānti bhūtāni saṃbhavam tatas teṣāṃ mahābhūtaśabdo 'yam upapadyate
english: Bhṛgu said: From these the countless beings, vast in their reach, come into existence; therefore this name, the great elements, rightly belongs to them.

sanskrit: ceṣṭā vayūḥ kham ākāśam ūṣmāgniḥ salilaṃ dravaḥ pṛthivī cātra saṃghātaḥ śarīraṃ pāñcabhautikam
english: Motion is wind; the void is space; heat is fire; the fluid is water; and the solid mass here is earth — thus the body is composed of the five elements.

sanskrit: ity etaiḥ pañcabhir bhūtair yuktaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam śrotraṃ ghrāṇaṃ rasaḥ sparśo dṛṣṭiś cendriyasaṃjñitāḥ
english: Thus all that moves and all that is fixed is joined of these five elements; and hearing, smell, taste, touch, and sight are what we call the senses.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca pañcabhir yadi bhūtais tu yuktāḥ sthāvarajaṅgamāḥ sthāvarāṇāṃ na dṛśyante śarīre pañca dhātavaḥ
english: Bharadvāja said: If both the moving and the unmoving are joined of the five elements, why are the five elements not seen in the bodies of unmoving things?

sanskrit: anūṣmaṇām aceṣṭānāṃ ghanānāṃ caiva tattvataḥ vṛkṣāṇāṃ nopalabhyante śarīre pañca dhātavaḥ
english: In trees, which in truth are without heat, without motion, and dense, the five elements are not perceived within their bodies.

sanskrit: na śṛṇvanti na paśyanti na gandharasavedinaḥ na ca sparśaṃ vijānanti te kathaṃ pāñcabhautikāḥ
english: They do not hear, they do not see, they perceive neither smell nor taste, and they do not know touch; how then are they composed of the five elements?

sanskrit: adravatvād anagnitvād abhaumatvād avāyutaḥ ākāśasyāprameyatvād vṛkṣāṇāṃ nāsti bhautikam
english: Being without fluidity, without fire, without earthiness, without wind, and since space is immeasurable in them, trees seem to have no elemental composition at all.

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca ghanānām api vṛkṣāṇām ākāśo 'sti na saṃśayaḥ teṣāṃ puṣpaphale vyaktir nityaṃ samupalabhyate
english: Bhṛgu said: Even in dense trees there is space, without doubt; its manifestation is ever observed in their flowers and fruits.

sanskrit: ūṣmato glānaparṇānāṃ tvak phalaṃ puṣpam eva ca mlāyate caiva śīte na sparśas tenātra vidyate
english: From heat, in trees whose leaves are wilting, the bark, fruit, and flower wither, and again in cold they fade; so it is not the case that touch is absent in them.

sanskrit: vāyvagnyaśaniniṣpeṣaiḥ phalapuṣpaṃ viśīryate śrotreṇa gṛhyate śabdas tasmāc chṛṇvanti pādapāḥ
english: By the buffeting of wind, fire, and lightning their fruit and flower fall away; sound is grasped by the organ of hearing, and therefore trees do hear.

sanskrit: vallī veṣṭayate vṛkṣaṃ sarvataś caiva gacchati na hy adṛṣṭeś ca mārgo 'sti tasmāt paśyanti pādapāḥ
english: A creeper coils about a tree and goes everywhere over it; but for one without sight there is no way to find its path, therefore trees do see.

sanskrit: puṇyāpuṇyais tathā gandhair dhūpaiś ca vividhair api arogāḥ puṣpitāḥ santi tasmāj jighranti pādapāḥ
english: By scents both pure and impure, and by various fragrant smokes, trees grow healthy and come to bloom; therefore trees do smell.

sanskrit: pādaiḥ salilapānaṃ ca vyādhīnām api darśanam vyādhipratikriyatvāc ca vidyate rasanaṃ drume
english: By its roots a tree drinks water, and it shows signs of sickness too; and since it can be treated for disease, the sense of taste exists in the tree.

sanskrit: vaktreṇotpalanālena yathordhvaṃ jalam ādadet tathā pavanasaṃyuktaḥ pādaiḥ pibati pādapaḥ
english: Just as one might draw water upward through the mouth of a lotus-stalk, so the tree, joined with the wind within it, drinks through its roots.

sanskrit: grahaṇāt sukhaduḥkhasya chinnasya ca virohaṇāt jīvaṃ paśyāmi vṛkṣāṇām acaitanyaṃ na vidyate
english: From their capacity to feel pleasure and pain, and from the resprouting of what has been cut, I perceive that trees possess life; insentience is not their condition.

sanskrit: tena taj jalam ādattaṃ jarayaty agnimārutau āhārapariṇāmāc ca sneho vṛddhiś ca jāyate
english: That water which is thus drawn up is digested by the fire and wind within, and from the transformation of this nourishment arise sap and growth.

sanskrit: jaṅgamānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ śarīre pañca dhātavaḥ pratyekaśaḥ prabhidyante yaiḥ śarīraṃ viceṣṭate
english: In the bodies of all moving creatures the five elements are present and are each severally distinguished, by which the body is set in motion.

sanskrit: tvak ca māṃsaṃ tathāsthīni majjā snāyu ca pañcamam ity etad iha saṃkhyātaṃ śarīre pṛthivīmayam
english: Skin, flesh, bones, marrow, and sinew as the fifth — these are reckoned here to be the earthy portion in the body.

sanskrit: tejo 'gniś ca tathā krodhaś cakṣur ūṣmā tathaiva ca agnir jarayate cāpi pañcāgneyāḥ śarīriṇaḥ
english: Vital heat, fire, anger, the eye, and bodily warmth, and the fire that digests as well — these five are the fiery elements in embodied beings.

sanskrit: śrotraṃ ghrāṇam athāsyaṃ ca hṛdayaṃ koṣṭham eva ca ākāśāt prāṇinām ete śarīre pañca dhātavaḥ
english: The ear, the nose, the mouth, the heart, and the belly's hollow — these five constituents arise from space in the bodies of living creatures.

sanskrit: śleṣmā pittam atha svedo vasā śoṇitam eva ca ity āpaḥ pañcadhā dehe bhavanti prāṇināṃ sadā
english: Phlegm, bile, sweat, fat, and blood — thus water is present fivefold in the body of living beings at all times.

sanskrit: prāṇāt praṇīyate prāṇī vyānād vyāyacchate tathā gacchaty apāno 'vāk caiva samāno hṛdy avasthitaḥ
english: By the prāṇa breath the living being is sustained; by the vyāna it exerts itself; the apāna passes downward and out; and the samāna abides in the heart.

sanskrit: udānād ucchvasiti ca pratibhedāc ca bhāṣate ity ete vāyavaḥ pañca ceṣṭayantīha dehinam
english: By the udāna one breathes out, and by its distinct workings one speaks; these are the five vital airs that set the embodied being in motion here.

sanskrit: bhūmer gandhaguṇān vetti rasaṃ cādbhyaḥ śarīravān jyotiḥ paśyati cakṣurbhyāṃ sparśaṃ vetti ca vāyunā
english: The embodied one knows the property of scent from earth, and flavor from water; it sees light with its eyes, and knows touch by means of wind.

sanskrit: tasya gandhasya vakṣyāmi vistarābhihitān guṇān iṣṭaś cāniṣṭagandhaś ca madhuraḥ kaṭur eva ca
english: Of that scent I shall declare the qualities set forth in full: the pleasant and the unpleasant scent, the sweet, and likewise the pungent,

sanskrit: nirhārī saṃhataḥ snigdho rūkṣo viśada eva ca evaṃ navavidho jñeyaḥ pārthivo gandhavistaraḥ
english: the penetrating, the compact, the unctuous, the dry, and the clear — thus the range of earthly scent is to be known as ninefold.

sanskrit: śabdaḥ sparśaś ca rūpaṃ ca rasaś cāpāṃ guṇāḥ smṛtāḥ rasajñānaṃ tu vakṣyāmi tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
english: Sound, touch, form, and flavor are held to be the qualities of water; now I shall declare the knowledge of flavor — hear it from me as I speak.

sanskrit: raso bahuvidhaḥ proktaḥ sūribhiḥ prathitātmabhiḥ madhuro lavaṇas tiktaḥ kaṣāyo 'mlaḥ kaṭus tathā eṣa ṣaḍvidhavistāro raso vārimayaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Flavor is declared to be of many kinds by the wise of renowned mind: sweet, salty, bitter, astringent, sour, and pungent; this is the sixfold range of flavor, held to consist of water.

sanskrit: śabdaḥ sparśaś ca rūpaṃ ca triguṇaṃ jyotir ucyate jyotiḥ paśyati rūpāṇi rūpaṃ ca bahudhā smṛtam
english: Light is said to have three qualities: sound, touch, and form; by light one sees forms, and form is held to be of many kinds.

sanskrit: hrasvo dīrghas tathā sthūlaś caturasro 'ṇu vṛttavān śuklaḥ kṛṣṇas tathā rakto nīlaḥ pīto 'ruṇas tathā evaṃ dvādaśavistāro jyotīrūpaguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Short, long, large, square, minute, round; white, black, red, blue, yellow, and tawny — thus the quality of form belonging to light is held to be twelvefold.

sanskrit: śabdasparśau tu vijñeyau dviguṇo vāyur ucyate vāyavyas tu guṇaḥ sparśaḥ sparśaś ca bahudhā smṛtaḥ
english: Wind is said to have two qualities, which are to be known as sound and touch; the quality proper to wind is touch, and touch is held to be of many kinds.

sanskrit: kaṭhinaś cikkaṇaḥ ślakṣṇaḥ picchalo mṛdudāruṇaḥ uṣṇaḥ śītaḥ sukho duḥkhaḥ snigdho viśada eva ca evaṃ dvādaśavistāro vāyavyo guṇa ucyate
english: Hard, smooth, sleek, slimy, soft, rough, hot, cold, pleasant, painful, unctuous, and clear — thus the quality belonging to wind is said to be twelvefold.

sanskrit: tatraikaguṇam ākāśaṃ śabda ity eva tat smṛtam tasya śabdasya vakṣyāmi vistaraṃ vividhātmakam
english: Among these, space has but a single quality, which is held to be sound alone; of that sound I shall declare the manifold range.

sanskrit: ṣaḍja ṛṣabhagāndhārau madhyamaḥ pañcamas tathā dhaivataś cāpi vijñeyas tathā cāpi niṣādakaḥ
english: Ṣaḍja, ṛṣabha and gāndhāra, madhyama and pañcama, and dhaivata likewise are to be known, and so too the niṣāda.

sanskrit: eṣa saptavidhaḥ prokto guṇa ākāśalakṣaṇaḥ traisvaryeṇa tu sarvatra sthito 'pi paṭahādiṣu
english: This quality, the mark of space, is declared to be sevenfold; yet through its three registers it abides everywhere, even in drums and the like.

sanskrit: ākāśajaṃ śabdam āhur ebhir vāyuguṇaiḥ saha avyāhataiś cetayate na vetti viṣamāgataiḥ
english: Sound, they say, is born of space together with these qualities of wind; one becomes aware of it when the airs come unobstructed, but knows it not when they come awry.

sanskrit: āpyāyante ca te nityaṃ dhātavas tais tu dhātubhiḥ āpo 'gnir mārutaś caiva nityaṃ jāgrati dehiṣu
english: These constituents are ever nourished by those constituents; and water, fire, and wind are ever awake within embodied beings.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca pārthivaṃ dhātum āśritya śārīro 'gniḥ kathaṃ bhavet avakāśaviśeṣeṇa kathaṃ vartayate 'nilaḥ
english: Bharadvāja said: Resting upon the earthy element, how does the fire of the body come to be? And by what distinct apportionment of space does the wind carry on its work?

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca vāyor gatim ahaṃ brahman kīrtayiṣyāmi te 'nagha prāṇinām anilo dehān yathā ceṣṭayate balī
english: Bhṛgu said: O brāhmaṇa, O sinless one, I shall recount to you the movement of the wind, and how the mighty air sets the bodies of living creatures in motion.

sanskrit: śrito mūrdhānam agnis tu śarīraṃ paripālayan prāṇo mūrdhani cāgnau ca vartamāno viceṣṭate
english: Fire, resting in the head, guards over the body; and the prāṇa breath, moving in the head and in that fire, sets all in motion.

sanskrit: sa jantuḥ sarvabhūtātmā puruṣaḥ sa sanātanaḥ mano buddhir ahaṃkāro bhūtāni viṣayāś ca saḥ
english: That living being is the Self of all beings; he is the eternal Person; he is mind, intellect, and ego-sense, the elements, and their objects.

sanskrit: evaṃ tv iha sa sarvatra prāṇena paripālyate pṛṣṭhataś ca samānena svāṃ svāṃ gatim upāśritaḥ
english: Thus here he is everywhere sustained by the prāṇa, and by the samāna from behind, each air abiding in its own proper course.

sanskrit: vastimūlaṃ gudaṃ caiva pāvakaṃ ca samāśritaḥ vahan mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ cāpy apānaḥ parivartate
english: Resting upon the base of the bladder, the rectum, and the digestive fire, the apāna circulates, bearing away urine and excrement.

sanskrit: prayatne karmaṇi bale ya ekas triṣu vartate udāna iti taṃ prāhur adhyātmaviduṣo janāḥ
english: That single one which operates in the three — in effort, in action, and in strength — they who know the inner Self call the udāna.

sanskrit: saṃdhiṣv api ca sarveṣu saṃniviṣṭas tathānilaḥ śarīreṣu manuṣyāṇāṃ vyāna ity upadiśyate
english: And the air that is set within all the joints in the bodies of men is taught to be the vyāna.

sanskrit: dhātuṣv agnis tu vitataḥ samānena samīritaḥ rasān dhātūṃś ca doṣāṃś ca vartayann avatiṣṭhati
english: The fire diffused throughout the bodily constituents, driven on by the samāna, abides there, setting the chyles, the constituents, and the humors in their course.

sanskrit: apānaprāṇayor madhye prāṇāpānasamāhitaḥ samanvitaḥ svadhiṣṭhānaḥ samyak pacati pāvakaḥ
english: Between the apāna and the prāṇa, joined together with prāṇa and apāna, well established in its own seat, the digestive fire thoroughly cooks the food.

sanskrit: āsyaṃ hi pāyusaṃyuktam ante syād gudasaṃjñitam srotas tasmāt prajāyante sarvasrotāṃsi dehinām
english: The mouth is joined with the anal passage, which at its end is called the rectum, the channel; from this arise all the channels of embodied beings.

sanskrit: prāṇānāṃ saṃnipātāc ca saṃnipātaḥ prajāyate ūṣmā cāgnir iti jñeyo yo 'nnaṃ pacati dehinām
english: And from the meeting together of the vital airs their concourse arises; what is to be known as heat and fire is that which cooks the food of embodied beings.

sanskrit: agnivegavahaḥ prāṇo gudānte pratihanyate sa ūrdhvam āgamya punaḥ samutkṣipati pāvakam
english: The prāṇa, borne on the rush of fire, is checked at the end of the rectum; then, coming back upward, it again casts up the digestive fire.

sanskrit: pakvāśayas tv adho nābher ūrdhvam āmāśayaḥ sthitaḥ nābhimadhye śarīrasya sarve prāṇāḥ samāhitāḥ
english: The seat of the digested food lies below the navel, the seat of the undigested above it; in the midmost navel of the body all the vital airs are gathered.

sanskrit: prasṛtā hṛdayāt sarve tiryag ūrdhvam adhas tathā vahanty annarasān nāḍyo daśa prāṇapracoditāḥ
english: Spread out from the heart, sideways, upward, and downward, the ten vessels, impelled by the vital breath, carry the chyle of food.

sanskrit: eṣa mārgo 'tha yogānāṃ yena gacchanti tat padam jitaklamāsanā dhīrā mūrdhany ātmānam ādadhuḥ
english: This is the path of the yogins, by which they reach that supreme station; steadfast, with weariness conquered and posture mastered, they have placed the Self within the head.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarveṣu vihitaḥ prāṇāpāneṣu dehinām tasmin sthito nityam agniḥ sthālyām iva samāhitaḥ
english: Thus the fire is set within all the prāṇas and apānas of embodied beings, abiding there forever, as one gathered within a cooking-pot.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca yadi prāṇāyate vāyur vāyur eva viceṣṭate śvasity ābhāṣate caiva tasmāj jīvo nirarthakaḥ
english: Bharadvāja said: If it is the wind that breathes, the wind alone that moves, that breathes and that speaks, then the soul is of no purpose at all.

sanskrit: yady ūṣmabhāva āgneyo vahninā pacyate yadi agnir jarayate caiva tasmāj jīvo nirarthakaḥ
english: If the state of heat is of fire, if it is by fire that the food is cooked, and if it is fire that digests, then the soul is of no purpose at all.

sanskrit: jantoḥ pramīyamāṇasya jīvo naivopalabhyate vāyur eva jahāty enam ūṣmabhāvaś ca naśyati
english: When a creature is dying, no soul is found to be present; the wind alone forsakes it, and its state of warmth perishes.

sanskrit: yadi vātopamo jīvaḥ saṃśleṣo yadi vāyunā vāyumaṇḍalavad dṛśyo gacchet saha marudgaṇaiḥ
english: If the soul were like the wind, if it were but conjunction with the wind, it would be visible like a whirl of air and would go off together with the troops of winds.

sanskrit: śleṣo yadi ca vātena yadi tasmāt praṇaśyati mahārṇavavimuktatvād anyat salilabhājanam
english: And if it is a conjunction with the wind, and if for that reason it perishes — then it is like another vessel of water poured out from the great ocean.

sanskrit: kūpe vā salilaṃ dadyāt pradīpaṃ vā hutāśane prakṣiptaṃ naśyati kṣipraṃ yathā naśyaty asau tathā
english: Or as water poured into a well, or a lamp cast into the fire, is swiftly lost when thrown in, even so does that soul perish.

sanskrit: pañcasādhāraṇe hy asmiñ śarīre jīvitaṃ kutaḥ yeṣām anyataratyāgāc caturṇāṃ nāsti saṃgrahaḥ
english: In this body, which is the common ground of the five, whence comes life — when, by the loss of any one of them, there is no holding together of the remaining four?

sanskrit: naśyanty āpo hy anāhārād vāyur ucchvāsanigrahāt naśyate koṣṭhabhedāt kham agnir naśyaty abhojanāt
english: Water perishes from want of food, the wind from the stopping of breath; space perishes from the breaking of the body's cavity, and fire perishes from lack of nourishment.

sanskrit: vyādhivraṇaparikleśair medinī caiva śīryate pīḍite 'nyatare hy eṣāṃ saṃghāto yāti pañcadhā
english: And the earthy element wastes away through disease, wounds, and afflictions; when any one of these is injured, the aggregate breaks apart fivefold.

sanskrit: tasmin pañcatvam āpanne jīvaḥ kim anudhāvati kiṃ vedayati vā jīvaḥ kiṃ śṛṇoti bravīti vā
english: When that body has dissolved into its five elements, what does the soul run after? What does the soul feel, or what does it hear or speak?

sanskrit: eṣā gauḥ paralokasthaṃ tārayiṣyati mām iti yo dattvā mriyate jantuḥ sā gauḥ kaṃ tārayiṣyati
english: "This cow will carry me across when I am in the world beyond" — but when the creature who gives her dies, whom shall that cow carry across?

sanskrit: gauś ca pratigrahītā ca dātā caiva samaṃ yadā ihaiva vilayaṃ yānti kutas teṣāṃ samāgamaḥ
english: When the cow, the receiver, and the giver alike go to their dissolution here in this very world, whence shall there be any meeting of them again?

sanskrit: vihagair upayuktasya śailāgrāt patitasya vā agninā copayuktasya kutaḥ saṃjīvanaṃ punaḥ
english: For one consumed by birds, or fallen from a mountain peak, or devoured by fire, whence shall there be any coming back to life again?

sanskrit: chinnasya yadi vṛkṣasya na mūlaṃ pratirohati bījāny asya pravartante mṛtaḥ kva punar eṣyati
english: If, when a tree is felled, the root does not sprout again, yet its seeds carry on — but the dead man, where shall he come again?

sanskrit: bījamātraṃ purā sṛṣṭaṃ yad etat parivartate mṛtā mṛtāḥ praṇaśyanti bījād bījaṃ pravartate
english: Only the seed, created in the beginning, is what carries on; the dead, once dead, utterly perish — from seed alone does seed proceed.
